segs.en: According to some authorities, there is a separate obligation to wash hands prior to prayer. One who washes and says the blessing of Al Netilat Yadayim after waking, does not repeat the blessing when washing prior to prayer.
segs.he: 317 לפי חלק מהפוסקים, ישנה חובה נפרדת של נטילת ידיים לפני התפילה [ערוה"ש או"ח, ד: ה]. מי שנטל ואמר ברכת על נטילת ידיים לאחר קימה משינה, אינו חוזר על הברכה בנטילה לפני התפילה [רמ"א או"ח, ו: ב].
segs.cite: ערוה"ש או"ח, ד: ה; רמ"א או"ח, ו: ב
segs.text: 317 According to some authorities, there is a separate obligation to wash hands prior to prayer [ערוה"ש או"ח, ד: ה]. One who washes and says the blessing of עַל נְְטִילַת יָדָֽיִם after waking, does not repeat the blessing when washing prior to prayer [רמ"א או"ח, ו: ב].

segs.en: Hands should preferably be washed using a cup, but a cup is not required. The custom is to pour water from the cup onto the right hand, then the left, and repeat a total of three times. Where water is unavailable, one may clean one’s hands using any appropriate material; in that case, the blessing is changed to Al Nekiut Yadayim.
segs.he: 318 עדיף לשטוף את הידיים בכוס, אך אין חובה בכוס [שו"ע ורמ"א, או"ח: ד, ז]. המנהג הוא לשפוך מים מהכוס על היד הימנית, ואז על השמאלית, ולחזור על כך שלוש פעמים [משנ"ב, שם: י]. במקום שאין בו מים, רשאי אדם לנקות את ידיו בכל חומר מתאים; ובמקרה זה, הברכה היא עַל נְקִיּוּת יָדָיִם [שו"ע או"ח, ד: כב].
segs.cite: שו"ע ורמ"א, או"ח: ד, ז; משנ"ב, שם: י; שו"ע או"ח, ד: כב
segs.text: 318 Hands should preferably be washed using a cup, but a cup is not required [שו"ע ורמ"א, או"ח: ד, ז]. The custom is to pour water from the cup onto the right hand, then the left, and repeat a total of three times [משנ"ב, שם: י]. Where water is unavailable, one may clean one’s hands using any appropriate material; in that case, the blessing is changed to עַל נְְקִיּוּת יָדָֽיִם [שו"ע או"ח, ד: כב].

segs.en: The blessing of Al Netilat Yadayim may be said before drying one’s hands or afterward.
segs.he: 319 ברכת על נטילת ידיים ניתן לומר לפני ייבוש הידיים או אחריהן [משנ"ב, ד: ב].
segs.cite: משנ"ב, ד: ב
segs.text: 319 The blessing of עַל נְְטִילַת יָדָֽיִם may be said before drying one’s hands or afterward [משנ"ב, ד: ב].

segs.en: A number of reasons have been offered for washing hands upon waking. The Gemara states that, during the night, hands are enveloped by an “evil vapor,” Ruach Ra'ah, which is removed by washing one’s hands. In addition, there is a concern that, while sleeping, one’s hands may have touched an unclean part of the body. Finally, it is noted that a person who wakes is like a newborn; therefore, one needs to sanctify oneself by washing.
segs.he: 320 ניתנו טעמים רבים לרעיית ידיים בשעת הקימה. הגמרא מציינת כי בלילה עוטפות הידיים "רוח רעה", אשר נשטפת על ידי רעיית הידיים [שבת, קח:]. בנוסף, יש חשש שבעת השינה יגעו הידיים באיבר טמא [רא"ש ברכות, פ"ט: כג]. ואף נאמר כי הקם משנתו כנולד; לכן עליו להטהר את עצמו ברעיית הידיים [שו"ת רשב"א ח"א, קצא].
segs.cite: שבת, קח:; רא"ש ברכות, פ"ט: כג; שו"ת רשב"א ח"א, קצא
segs.text: 320 A number of reasons have been offered for washing hands upon waking. The Gemara states that, during the night, hands are enveloped by an “evil vapor,” רוח רעה, which is removed by washing one’s hands [שבת, קח:]. In addition, there is a concern that, while sleeping, one’s hands may have touched an unclean part of the body [רא"ש ברכות, פ"ט: כג]. Finally, it is noted that a person who wakes is like a newborn; therefore, one needs to sanctify oneself by washing [שו"ת רשב"א ח"א, קצא].

segs.en: The blessing of Asher Yatzar should be said each time after relieving oneself. It is recommended that one should go to the bathroom immediately after washing hands, then say the blessings of Al Netilat Yadayim followed by Asher Yatzar. However, even if one does not relieve oneself, one is permitted to say Asher Yatzar after washing hands. One should not postpone going to the bathroom.
segs.he: 321 יש לומר ברכת אשר יצר בכל פעם שאדם משתחרר מהיטלה. מומלץ ללכת לשירותים מיד לאחר נטילת ידיים, ואז לומר את ברכות על נטילת ידיים ואחריהן אשר יצר. אולם, גם אם לא השתחרר, רשאי לומר אשר יצר לאחר נטילת ידיים [רמ"א או"ח, ד: א]. אין לעכב את ההשתחררות [שו"ע או"ח, ג: יז].
segs.cite: רמ"א או"ח, ד: א; שו"ע או"ח, ג: יז
segs.text: 321 The blessing of אֲשֶׁר יָצַר should be said each time after relieving oneself. It is recommended that one should go to the bathroom immediately after washing hands, then say the blessings of עַל נְְטִילַת יָדָֽיִם followed by אֲשֶׁר יָצַר. However, even if one does not relieve oneself, one is permitted to say אֲשֶׁר יָצַר after washing hands [רמ"א או"ח, ד: א]. One should not postpone going to the bathroom [שו"ע או"ח, ג: יז].

segs.en: According to the Gemara, the blessing of Elokai Neshama should be said upon waking. The contemporary custom is to say Elokai Neshama immediately after Asher Yatzar. However, some rule that one who stays up all night should not say Elokai Neshama and the blessing HaMevir Shana Mei'enei, and should instead hear them from others.
segs.he: 322 על פי הגמרא, ברכת אלהי נשמה יש לומר בעת הקימה [ברכות, ס:]. המנהג כיום הוא לומר אלהי נשמה מיד אחרי אשר יצר [משנ"ב, שם: יב]. אולם, יש אומרים שמי שישן כל הלילה אינו צריך לומר אלהי נשמה וברכת המעביר שינה מעיני, אלא לשמוע אותן מאחרים [משנ"ב, מו: כד].
segs.cite: ברכות, ס:; משנ"ב, שם: יב; משנ"ב, מו: כד
segs.text: 322 According to the Gemara, the blessing of אֱלֹהַי נְְשָׁמָה should be said upon waking [ברכות, ס:]. The contemporary custom is to say אֱלֹהַי נְְשָׁמָה immediately after אֲשֶׁר יָצַר [משנ"ב, שם: יב]. However, some rule that one who stays up all night should not say אֱלֹהַי נְְשָׁמָה and the blessing הַמַּעֲבִיר שֵׁנָה מֵעֵינַי, and should instead hear them from others [משנ"ב, מו: כד].

The accepted practice is to wear a tallit katan all day long and to wear a tallit gadol during Shaḥarit. The dominant Ashkenazi custom is to begin wearing a tallit gadol when one marries, but Jews of German and Sephardi descent begin wearing the tallit gadol at an earlier age. Nevertheless, the custom is to wear a tallit gadol – even if unmarried – when acting as Shaliaḥ Tzibbur, reading from or being called up to the Torah, opening the Ark or performing hagbaha or gelila.

parts.en: The tefillin shel yad is put on first, by placing the box on the biceps near the elbow joint, angled toward the heart, and saying the blessing Lehanot Tefillin. One then tightens the strap around the muscle and wraps the strap around the forearm seven times. Without speaking or otherwise becoming distracted, one places the tefillin shel rosh on the head above the hairline, centered over the nose, and says the blessing Al Mitzvat Tefillin. One then adjusts the straps, so that the knot rests at the base of the skull and the two straps hang down the front of one’s chest, and says Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto LeOlam Va'ed. Finally, one wraps the strap of the tefillin shel yad around the fingers, while saying Va'Arashticha (See page 17).

parts.en: At a minimum, tefillin should be worn while saying the Shema and the Amida. The custom is to keep them on until one has heard the Kedusha three times and Kaddish four times, which means that one should not remove the tefillin until after the Mourner’s Kaddish following Aleinu. In theory, one should wear tefillin all day. The custom, however, is to take the tefillin off after praying, because it is difficult to maintain a constant awareness of the tefillin and the requisite purity of mind and body throughout the day.

The insertion of the verse (or verses) of Shema after Birkhot HaShaḥar was not meant to satisfy the individual’s obligation to say the Shema every morning. However, as discussed in further detail in law 347, the three paragraphs of Shema must be said within the first half of the morning (measured as ¼ of the time from daybreak to nightfall). Since some congregations hold Shaḥarit services late, especially on Shabbat, and as such the communal recitation of the Shema in Shaḥarit may take place too late to fulfill the halakhic obligation, under such circumstances it is recommended to say all three paragraphs of Shema after Birkhot HaShaḥar.

There is a set time period every morning during which the Shema may be said. The optimal time is immediately before sunrise, when there is assumed to be sufficient light to recognize an acquaintance from a distance of four amot (around 6 feet). If necessary, the Shema may be said from daybreak. After sunrise, the earlier the Shema is said, the better. At the latest, the Shema must be said during the first quarter of the day (in halakhic terminology, three halakhic “hours,” where each hour represents 1/12 of the day; regarding the measure of a “day,” see law 204). After that time, one is permitted to say the Shema with the blessings during the fourth halakhic “hour,” that is, until the end of the first third of the day. After that, the Shema may be said without the blessings, but this does not fulfill the mitzva.

parts.en: There is a set time period every morning during which the Amida may be said. In general, the Amida should be said at or after sunrise. At the latest, the Amida should be said during the first third of the day, (four halakhic “hours”; regarding the measure of a “day,” see law 204). If the Amida was said between daybreak and sunrise, the mitzva has been fulfilled. If necessary, it is permissible to say the Amida after the first third of the day, but before midday.

segs.en: One who must leave for work (or a journey) before sunrise is permitted to say the Amida from daybreak. If one did not say the Shaḥarit Amida prior to midday, one should say the Minḥa Amida twice.
segs.he: 357 מי שצריך לצאת לעבודה (או למסע) לפני הנץ החמה רשאי לומר עמידה עם עלות השחר [שו"ע שם סע' ח]. מי שלא אמר עמידת שחרית לפני הצהריים, צריך לומר עמידת מנחה פעמיים [משנ"ב, שם: ס"ק ז].

segs.en: One should not eat or drink before saying the Amida, although drinking water is permitted. Moreover, anyone who needs to eat or drink in order to concentrate on his prayers is permitted to do so.
segs.he: 358 אין לאכול או לשתות לפני אמירת עמידה, אלא שרשות לשתות מים. יתרה מכך, כל הצורך לאכול או לשתות כדי להתרכז בתפילתו, רשאי לעשות כן [שו"ע או"ח, פט: ג–ד].

segs.en: The Amida is said facing the site of the Temple in Jerusalem. Thus, outside Israel, one faces the land of Israel; inside Israel, one faces Jerusalem; and inside Jerusalem, one faces the Temple Mount. If one is praying in a synagogue, one should pray facing the Ark.
segs.he: 359 העמידה נאמרת כשהאדם פונה לכיוון מקום המקדש בירושלים. לכן, מחוץ לארץ פונים לכיוון ארץ ישראל; בתוך ארץ ישראל פונים לירושלים; ובתוך ירושלים פונים להר הבית [שו"ע או"ח צד: א]. אם מתפללים בבית כנסת, יש לפנות לכיוון הארון [משנ"ב שם: ס"ק י].

If one is praying in a synagogue, one should pray facing the Ark [משנ"ב, שם: ס"ק י].

segs.en: The Amida is said standing with feet together in imitation of the angels who, according to tradition, present the appearance of having only one leg. One should bow one’s head and imagine one is standing in the Temple, like a servant before his master.
segs.he: 360 העמידה נאמרת בעמידה כשהרגליים צמודות, כחידוש המלאכים אשר לפי המסורת נראים כאילו יש להם רגל אחת בלבד [ברכות י, רש"י ד"ה ״ורגליהם״]. יש להוריד את הראש ולדמיין שמתפללים במקדש, כעבד לפני אדוניו [שו"ע או"ח צה: א–ב].

441 Candle lighting: At least two candles are lit [שו"ע או"ח, רסג: א]. There is a custom to light one candle for each member of the household. segs.en: The custom is to light Shabbat candles 18 minutes prior to sunset. In any case, the candles must be lit before sunset, at which time all labor must cease. After lighting the candles, one may not perform any labor, even if one lit prior to sunset, unless one's intention to perform necessary labor before sunset is articulated explicitly prior to lighting.
segs.he: 442 המנהג הוא להדליק נרות שבת 18 דקות לפני השקיעה. בכל מקרה, יש להדליק את הנרות לפני השקיעה, שבה יש להפסיק כל מלאכה [שו"ע ורמ"א או"ח, רסא: א]. לאחר הדלקת הנרות, אסור לאדם לעשות מלאכה, גם אם הדליק לפני השקיעה, אלא אם כן כוונתו לעשות מלאכה נחוצה לפני השקיעה נאמרה במפורש לפני ההדלקה [רמ"א או"ח, רסג: י; משנ"ב, שם: מב].

segs.text:
A HALAKHIC GUIDE TO PRAYER FOR VISITORS TO ISRAEL
GENERAL RULES PUBLIC VS. PRIVATE CONDUCT
473 For halakhic purposes, the definition of “visitor” is one who intends to return to his place of origin within one year [משנ"ב, קיז: ה]. Unmarried students may be considered visitors as long as they are supported by their parents [שו"ת אגרות משה או"ח ח"ב, קא].

segs.en: General rule: Visitors follow their own customs in private, but follow local Israeli practice in public to avoid deviation.
segs.he: 474 ככלל, על מבקר בארץ להמשיך לעשות כנהוגו בפרטיות. אולם בציבור, יש להימנע מהנהגה השונה מהנהגות המקום [שו"ע או"ח, תסח: ד; משנ"ב, שם: יד]. לכן, על המבקר בארץ לנהוג בדרך כלל לפי מנהגו, וזאת מוגבל לתפילותיו הפרטיות בלבד.
segs.text: 474 In general, a visitor to Israel should continue to follow his or her customs in private. In public, however, one should avoid conduct that deviates from local practice [שו"ע או"ח, תסח: ד; משנ"ב, שם: יד]. Hence, a visitor to Israel should generally pray in accordance with his non-Israeli customs. This rule is limited, however, to one’s private prayers.

segs.en: Residency for Purim is determined by presence at dawn on the 15th (Jerusalem) or 14th (outside). Some opinions rely on intention the preceding evening.

segs.text: 489 One is considered a resident of Jerusalem for these purposes if one is present in Jerusalem at dawn on the morning of the 15th of Adar. Similarly, one is considered a non-resident of Jerusalem for these purposes if one is outside Jerusalem at dawn on the 14th of Adar. There is, however, an opinion that the determining factor is one’s intention on the preceding evening [משנ"ב, תרפח: יג].

segs.en: Practical rule: Staying outside Jerusalem on Purim eve and inside on Shushan Purim eve obligates celebrating twice. Staying inside on Purim eve and outside on Shushan Purim eve may result in no obligation.
segs.text: 490 As a practical matter, a person who stays overnight outside Jerusalem on Purim eve, but stays overnight in Jerusalem on Shushan Purim eve, is obligated to celebrate Purim twice – first on the 14th of Adar, along with non-residents of Jerusalem, and then on the 15th of Adar, along with residents of Jerusalem. Conversely, a person who stays overnight in Jerusalem on Purim eve but stays overnight outside Jerusalem on Shushan Purim eve would have no obligation to celebrate Purim at all.
